newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mergers seen rising in Japan -- brokerage report.
newsitem.headline: Mergers seen rising in Japan -- brokerage report.

text.p: Mergers and acquisitions (M&A) involving Japanese firms are likely to rise by 75 to almost 700 cases this year, marking the fourth straight year of growth, a securities brokerage said in report on Thursday.
In the six months to June, M&A involving Japanese firms totalled 330, up 28 cases from the same period a year ago, said Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd, one of Japan's "Big Four" brokerages.
"After hitting bottom in 1993, the number of M&A increased for the third straight year in 1996 and this trend has been sustained so far this year," Yamaichi said.

The number of M&A among Japanese companies jumped by 46 cases to 203 in the six-month period, while the number of cases in which foreign firms, mostly American and Southeast Asian, bought stakes in or took over operations of Japanese firms totalled 33, up 11 from the same period a year ago, it said.

The number of cases in which Japanese firms bought stakes or took over operations of foreign firms dropped by 29 to 94, but Yamaichi said the fall was temporary and predicted an increase for the full year.
While Japanese companies' direct investment in the United States and Europe declined, their investment in Asian nations continued to grow, it added.
The report said the average spending in M&A cases involving Japanese firms stood at 7.1 billion yen in the January-June period, up 3.1 billion yen from the same period a year ago.
